names.official: Independent State of Papua New Guinea

summary: Papua New Guinea runs a free 60-day tourist eVisa for citizens of a long list of countries — including the US, UK, EU states, Australia, New Zealand, Japan and most of the Pacific — while other nationalities apply at a PNG mission abroad. Melanesian Spearhead Group neighbors enter visa-free.

notes: Firearms, ammunition and offensive weapons are prohibited without prior authorization.
Quarantine rules cover fresh food, seeds, plants, wooden artefacts and animal products — carved souvenirs may need treatment or a permit to take home.
Cultural artefacts and anything made from protected wildlife, including bird of paradise plumes, cannot be exported without a permit.

payments.text: Cards work in Port Moresby hotels, larger supermarkets and some resorts, but almost nowhere else. ATMs are concentrated in the towns and can be unsafe to use after dark. Carry kina in cash and keep it out of sight.

safety.text: Crime is a genuine concern, especially in Port Moresby and Lae, where carjacking, robbery and opportunistic street crime occur. Most visitors travel with pre-arranged transfers, avoid walking after dark, and stay clear of highlands areas affected by tribal violence. Rural and resort areas are generally calmer.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Papua New Guinea travel advice

bestTimeToVisit.text: May to October is the dry season — the window for the Kokoda Track, highlands festivals such as the Goroka and Mount Hagen shows, and reliable domestic flights.

tips.text: Arrange an airport transfer with your hotel before you land, do not walk in Port Moresby or Lae — including short distances in daylight — and keep car doors locked in traffic. Most incidents involving visitors happen on foot or at ATMs.

Apply for the tourist eVisa on the official ICA portal at evisa.ica.gov.pg at least two weeks out. Airlines will not board you on an eVisa nationality without the approval letter, and there is no reliable visa on arrival to fall back on.
Malaria is present nearly everywhere below 1,800 m and dengue occurs too. Start prophylaxis before you arrive, use repellent from dusk, and sleep under a net outside air-conditioned hotels.

There is no road network linking most of the country — Air Niugini and PNG Air domestic flights are the only practical way between regions, they fill up around festival dates, and delays are routine. Leave a buffer day before your international flight home.

Land and custom matter: ask permission before entering villages, photographing people or walking on clan land, and expect to pay a small fee for access to sites and trails. A local guide is both good manners and good security.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Papua New Guinea?
faq.answer: Most visitors do, but for a long list of nationalities — including the US, UK, EU states, Australia, New Zealand, Japan and much of the Pacific — it is a free 60-day tourist eVisa applied for online before you fly. Other nationalities apply for a visa at a PNG diplomatic mission, and Fijian, Solomon Islands and Vanuatu citizens enter visa-free.

faq.question: How do I apply for the PNG tourist eVisa?
faq.answer: Apply on the Immigration and Citizenship Authority portal at evisa.ica.gov.pg with a passport scan, photo, itinerary, accommodation details, onward ticket and proof of funds. Approval usually takes a few business days, and you carry the approval with you to check-in.

faq.question: Is there a visa on arrival in Papua New Guinea?
faq.answer: A limited visa on arrival has existed at Port Moresby's Jacksons International Airport for some nationalities and business travelers, but it has been suspended and reinstated repeatedly and airlines often refuse to board passengers relying on it. Treat the eVisa as the only dependable route and confirm with ICA if you plan otherwise.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Papua New Guinea?
faq.answer: The tourist eVisa allows up to 60 days per entry. Extensions are possible from inside the country through the Immigration and Citizenship Authority, but apply well before the visa expires — overstaying carries fines and removal.

faq.question: Is Papua New Guinea safe to visit?
faq.answer: It needs care rather than avoidance. Port Moresby and Lae have significant crime and parts of the highlands see tribal violence, so travelers use pre-arranged transport, avoid moving around after dark and often travel with a guide or operator. Dive resorts, Milne Bay, Tufi and the Sepik are generally calmer.

faq.question: What vaccinations do I need for Papua New Guinea?
faq.answer: A yellow fever certificate is required only if you arrive from a yellow fever risk country. Beyond that nothing is compulsory, but hepatitis A, typhoid and tetanus are commonly recommended, and malaria prophylaxis is important for almost all of the country.
